title: Jeva and the Decision Model: How Picking From a List Became Its Own Architecture
description: Jeva is an open 4-billion-parameter model that returns a choice, a probability or a score instead of text. Here is the line of classifiers it grew out of, how its decision head works, and what its results do and don't show.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 10: Prior Authorization
description: How a prior authorization request moves from provider to payer and back, the decision timelines in federal rules, what the 2024 CMS rule changes in 2026 and 2027, the electronic standards, and where reform and AI fit.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 11: Care Management
description: How payers try to keep members healthy and out of hospital: risk stratification, case and disease management, transitions after discharge, quality measures like HEDIS and Star Ratings, and the evidence on whether it saves money.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 12: From Visit to Claim
description: How a provider turns care into a claim: registration, documentation, charge capture and the chargemaster, coding, claim scrubbing, clearinghouses, acknowledgements and rejections, with one office visit followed end to end.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 13: Claim Adjudication
description: What happens inside a payer's system between receiving a claim and paying it: the adjudication pipeline step by step, coding edits, pricing, denials and their reason codes, pends, payment timing and corrected claims.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 14: The Claim SOP, Step by Step
description: The checks a claim examiner works through on a pended claim, in order, from eligibility and provider status through duplicates, authorization, coding, coordination of benefits and pricing, to a documented decision, with four worked cases and the appeal paths that follow.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 15: Payment Integrity
description: How payers find and recover wrong payments before and after they're made: improper payment rates, prepayment and post-payment review, clinical and coding validation, COB and subrogation recovery, fraud, waste and abuse, and risk adjustment audits.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 16: How Providers Get Paid
description: The payment methods behind US healthcare: Medicare's physician fee schedule and RVUs, DRGs and APCs, commercial rates as a multiple of Medicare, capitation, value-based contracts and bundles, and how CMS pays Medicare Advantage plans.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 17: Pharmacy and PBMs
description: How the drug benefit runs on its own rails: pharmacy benefit managers, formularies and tiers, real-time pharmacy claims, list prices and rebates, specialty drugs, the medical-versus-pharmacy split, and Medicare Part D's recent changes.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 18: The Data and Rules Underneath, and Where AI Fits
description: The transactions, privacy rules and interoperability standards that every part of US healthcare runs on, the data problems that cause most failures, and where AI helps, where it's risky, and what rules now govern it.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 3: Premiums, Cost Sharing and How a Plan Pays
description: Premiums, deductibles, copays, coinsurance and the out-of-pocket maximum, worked through one family's year of claims, plus networks, surprise bills and HSAs.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 4: The Code Systems
description: ICD-10 diagnoses, CPT and HCPCS procedures, modifiers, DRGs, revenue codes, NDCs and the identifiers that turn a doctor's visit into data a payer can process.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 5: Coverage Policy
description: How a plan decides whether a service is covered at all: Medicare's national and local coverage determinations, Medicare Advantage rules, commercial medical policies, and the criteria vendors behind them.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 6: Eligibility and Enrollment
description: How members get into a payer's system, how a provider checks coverage before a visit, what goes wrong with retroactive changes, and how two plans decide which pays first.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 7: Network Management
description: How payers build provider networks: contracting and rates, credentialing and primary source verification, the provider data behind directories and claims, and the rules on network adequacy.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 8: Benefit Digitization
description: How a health plan's benefits, written in documents for people, become configuration a claim system can run: service categories, cost-share rules, limits and authorization flags, and where it goes wrong.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 9: Utilization Management
description: How payers review whether care is medically necessary before, during and after it happens: prospective, concurrent and retrospective review, inpatient versus observation, who makes the decision, and where review goes wrong.

title: Kimi K3.1 and the Road From Softmax Attention to Kimi Delta Attention
description: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a 2.8-trillion-parameter open model in which three of every four attention layers keep a fixed-size memory instead of a growing KV cache. Here is how attention got there, step by step.

title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: Using a World Model to Catch Hijacked GUI Agents
description: A login screen is safe after tapping Sign in and suspicious after tapping View order. A new paper checks each step of a phone or browser agent by predicting the next screen in embedding space, and catches hijacks a screen-only monitor provably cannot.

title: Agent Skills, Explained: What They Are and How They Differ From MCP
description: Agent Skills became a vendor-neutral standard on 22 October 2026. Here is what a skill is, how agents load them without filling their context, and where they fit next to MCP.

title: Do AI Agents Need a Memory System? What Two New Papers Found
description: MemoryTax found that a strong model searching its raw history beat memory frameworks, and TurnCost found that an agent's bill grows with its turns, not with the size of tool output.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 1: Members, Patients, Providers and Payers
description: Who the players in US healthcare are, how many of each there are, and how money and information move between them when someone sees a doctor.

title: How US Healthcare Works, Part 2: Public and Private Coverage
description: Medicare and its four parts, Medicaid and CHIP, employer plans, the ACA marketplaces and the military and veterans' systems: who each one covers, who pays for it, and how it reaches providers.

title: From Image Classifiers to H-JEPA: Learning by Predicting What Matters
description: How vision models went from needing a label on every image to world models that plan by predicting in their own representation space, and what the new H-JEPA paper adds.
